decisions.decision: Vertex population is a generic finite type `V` with `[DecidableEq V] [Fintype V]`, and `p := Fintype.card V`. The core's `V = [p]` is realized as `Fintype.card V = p` rather than `Fin p`.
decisions.why: `Causalean.DAG V` is stated for exactly this signature, so the whole `Graph/MarkovEquiv/` substrate (skeleton, immoralities, covered-edge reversal, edge-difference count, Verma-Pearl flagship) applies verbatim. `Fin p` would force a transport layer for zero reuse gain. Every `p`-indexed claim (integer entries in `{0,...,p}`, denominator `<= p`, height `<= Nat.clog 2 p`, the `Nat.choose (p+1) 3` bound) is stated with `p = Fintype.card V`.

decisions.decision: The blocked-state class is a structure over a RAW edge relation (`edge : V -> V -> Prop`, `decEdge`) plus `blocks : V -> Finset (Finset V)`, with the two core assumption atoms as its only two Prop fields; a derived projection `BlockedState.toDAG := Causalean.DAG.ofAcyclic edge acyclic` exposes it as a `Causalean.DAG`.
decisions.why: P2 of the plan gate requires the class's `members` to be exactly `[ass:acyclic-member, ass:target-parent-partition]`. Embedding a bundled `Causalean.DAG` field would silently absorb `ass:acyclic-member` into the field's own invariant and destroy the author's atomization. Carrying the raw relation keeps both atoms as named `Prop` defs while `toDAG` recovers full substrate reuse.

decisions.decision: Parent partitions are encoded as `blocks : V -> Finset (Finset V)` constrained by the Prop atom `IsTargetParentPartition`, not as a bundled `Finpartition (G.parents j)`.
decisions.why: Mathlib's `Finpartition s` is a bundled TYPE whose index `s` depends on the graph field; an assumption atom must be one named `Prop` def. The atom is written in `Finpartition.ofExistsUnique` shape (`empty not a block`, `every parent in a unique block`) so a `Finpartition` can be produced on demand by a helper.

decisions.decision: The static signature is a decidable-equality record of `Finset` codings (`skeleton : Finset (V x V)` as unordered-pair coding, `colliders : Finset (V x V x V)`, `families : V -> Finset (Finset V)`, `mismatch : Finset (V x V)`), with bridge lemmas `staticSignature_eq_iff` tying its first two coordinates to `Causalean.SameSkeleton` / `Causalean.SameImmoralities`.
decisions.why: The theorems compare signatures by EQUALITY, which needs a `Finset` coding, while the reusable substrate (`markovEquiv_iff_sameSkeleton_sameImmoralities`, `exists_covered_reversed_edge`, `edgeDiffCount_flipEdge_lt`, `flipEdge_same*`) is stated for the propositional forms. The bridge lemma is the single adapter that unlocks all of it.

decisions.decision: `def:component-enumerator` is defined extensionally: `componentEnum C` is the `Finset` of canonical lifts `E_K` over acyclic `K` with `SameSkeleton G_C K`, `SameImmoralities G_C K` and `familyMismatchEdges C` retained as edges of `K`. The CPDAG + Meek-closure route named in the core is recorded as the algorithmic presentation of that same output set.
decisions.why: The core's own proof of `prop:exact-component-enumeration` uses only the extensional characterization ('each emitted K has the skeleton and colliders of G, retains F(C), and has the same endpoint families'). Causalean has no CPDAG / Meek-rule module (searched; only a prose mention in `Causalean/Graph/MarkovEquiv.lean`), so building the closure algorithm would add a large orientation-rule layer that the theorem never inspects. The `at most p!` termination claim is proved through the injection into topological orders exactly as in the core proof.

decisions.decision: The Bonferroni critical value in `def:simultaneous-region` is a chosen `z` satisfying `(Causalean.Stat.gaussianMeasure 0 1) (Set.Iic z) >= 1 - alpha/(2*K)`, obtained from a small existence lemma, rather than an inverse-CDF function.
decisions.why: Neither Mathlib nor Causalean exposes a standard-normal quantile function (searched: only `ProbabilityTheory.cdf`, `Causalean.Stat.CLT.GaussianTail`). Existence of such a `z` is all the coverage proof consumes, and `Causalean.Stat.Tendsto_dist.wald_coverage_Iic` is stated against a threshold `c`, not a quantile function.

decisions.decision: Rational bit height `hgt` uses `Nat.clog 2 (max 1 (max q.num.natAbs q.den))`; `Bp p = Nat.clog 2 p`.
decisions.why: `Nat.clog 2` is Mathlib's ceiling base-2 logarithm on naturals and matches the core's `ceil(log_2 .)` on positive integers exactly, avoiding real logarithms and their rounding lemmas.

env.world: Singleton-permitting blocked edge-coloured linear Gaussian DAG models over \(V\). A state \(E_0=(G_{E_0},\Pi^{E_0})\) pairs an acyclic graph on \(V\) with, for every target \(j\), a partition \(\Pi^{E_0}_j\) of \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_{E_0}}(j)\) into nonempty coefficient blocks, singletons permitted. Its parameter space is \(\Theta_{E_0}=\mathbb R^{b_{E_0}}\times(0,\infty)^p\) with \(b_{E_0}=\sum_j|\Pi^{E_0}_j|\): one unrestricted real coefficient per block and one positive innovation variance per vertex. The block-constant matrix \(B_{E_0}(\beta)\) has \((B_{E_0}(\beta))_{ji}=\beta_{jB}\) for \(i\in B\in\Pi^{E_0}_j\) and zero at nonparents, and the covariance map is \(\phi_{E_0}(\beta,\omega)=(I_p-B_{E_0}(\beta))^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\omega)(I_p-B_{E_0}(\beta))^{-\mathsf T}\), whose full image \(\mathcal M(E_0)\subseteq\mathbb S^p_{++}\) is the observational model. Population objects live over an arbitrary \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\): parent regressions \(r_j(P;\Sigma)=\Sigma_{P,P}^{-1}\Sigma_{P,j}\), block-constrained regressions, determinant and cleared-regression certificates, unit-noise binary-star covariances, and legal singleton covered reversals with partition transport. No probability space, no faithfulness assumption, no restriction to nonzero coefficients.
env.notes: The blocked (target-local edge-coloured) layer is genuinely new: no Causalean or Mathlib object carries a per-target partition of parent sets with block-constant structural coefficients. It is built ON TOP of S1 (`BlockedState.toDAG`) so the graph coordinate is never rebuilt. citations.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1 [Verma and Pearl, 1990] Two dags are equivalent if and only if they have the same skeletons and the same v-structures. Theorem 2 Let G and G' be any pair of dags such that G is equivalent to G'. There exists a sequence of |Delta(G,G')| distinct edge reversals in G with the following properties: (1) Each edge reversed in G is a covered edge. (2) After each reversal, G is a dag and G is equivalent to G'. (3) After all reversals, G = G'.
